notes_en: The most common verb root in Korean. 공부하다 (study-do = 'to study'), 운동하다 (exercise-do = 'to exercise'). Attach 하 to many noun concepts to form a verb.

gloss_en: casual ending after a dark vowel (ㅓ/ㅜ/ㅡ/ㅣ)
notes_en: Banmal (casual) ending. Pairs with 아 for vowel harmony. Used among close friends and to people younger than you.

gloss_en: casual ending after a bright vowel (ㅏ/ㅗ)
notes_en: Banmal counterpart of 어. 가 + 아 → 가, 좋 + 아 → 좋아.
Marks what you're talking about. 저는 = 'as for me'. Pairs with 은 for consonant endings. The hardest single grammar point for English speakers — contrast with 이/가.
Marks the new-information subject. 비가 와요 = 'rain is falling' (focus: rain). Pairs with 가 for vowel endings.
Marks the direct object. 책을 읽어요 = 'I read a book'. Pairs with 를 for vowel endings.
Same role as 이 but used after vowel endings. 친구가 와요 = 'a friend is coming'.

gloss_en: past-tense marker after a bright vowel
notes_en: Inserted between verb stem and final ending. 가 + 았 + 어요 → 갔어요 ('went').

gloss_en: past-tense marker after a dark vowel
notes_en: Pairs with 았. 먹 + 었 + 어요 → 먹었어요 ('ate').

gloss_en: 'to / at / in / on' — location or time
notes_en: Static location or destination. 학교에 가요 ('I go to school'). 세 시에 ('at 3 o'clock'). Different from 에서 (action's location).
Default polite form for strangers, classes, learners. 가요 ('go'), 먹어요 ('eat'). Always your safe choice.
Seeks agreement or implies shared understanding. 좋지? ('it's good, right?'). Also used as a connector ('and').
Consonant-ending counterpart of 는. 책은 ('as for the book').
Joins two verbs in sequence. 먹고 가요 ('eat and go'). Also: -고 있어요 = '-ing' (progressive).
Banmal sentence-final particle. 뭐야? ('what is it?'). With names → vocative: 'John아!' to call someone.
Marks possession. 친구의 책 ('a friend's book'). Often dropped in casual speech: 친구 책 also works.
Vowel-ending counterpart of 을. 김치를 좋아해요 ('I like kimchi').
Replaces 은/는 or 이/가 to add 'also'. 저도 가요 ('I'm going too').
Shows respect for the subject of the verb. 가시다 ('to go' — honorific). Common in formal speech and toward elders.
